comment: The LIMR governs logical models, and FHIR is recommended for exchange. Experience with national clinical information models (e.g. the Netherlands’ zibs, per ISO 13972) shows the translation from logical model to technical artefact (FHIR profile, storage model) is not inherently one-to-one; meaning can shift or be lost in that step even when systems are technically conformant.

public.text: The LIMR governs logical models, and FHIR is recommended for exchange. Experience with national clinical information models (e.g. the Netherlands’ zibs, per ISO 13972) shows the translation from logical model to technical artefact (FHIR profile, storage model) is not inherently one-to-one; meaning can shift or be lost in that step even when systems are technically conformant.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to §3.7 a requirement for semantic fidelity testing across the translation step: round-trip verification that data instantiated from a logical model, exchanged via its technical representation, and re-interpreted at the receiving end preserves the governed meaning — not only structural/technical conformance. Reference ISO 13972 for clinical information model quality requirements.
